evidence: His budget included $16.5 million in state funds to preserve the enhanced ACA tax credits for Hawaii families (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Has issued a rolling series of emergency proclamations on affordable housing since 2023; the twentieth was issued in July 2026.
Touted signing the most significant housing regulatory and zoning reforms in over 40 years (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Proposed pausing upper-end future tax cuts to reinvest about $600 million in food security and child care for working families (Jan 2026); not a universal system.
Signed SB 3025 (Act 220), creating a state program to buy and forgive medical debt for up to 50,000 residents (Jul 2026).
Says he directed more resources to Medicaid rate increases covering almost 400,000 people (Jan 2026 State of the State); Hawaii already expanded Medicaid.
Signed Act 46 (2024), billed as the largest income tax cut in state history; in May 2026 signed SB 3125 revising future steps but keeping most low/middle-income relief.
Cites doubling the state Earned Income Tax Credit and Food Tax Credit, saving families $88 million a year (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Signed HB 1890 (Act 233) setting salary step and longevity raises for educators (Jul 2026).
Signed Act 162 requiring written immigration-enforcement policies at protected community locations, plus Act 141 limiting ICE cooperation (Jul 2026); not a warrant-only ban.
Signed SB 1 (Act 2) as his first bill, expanding abortion access and shielding providers and patients in state law (Mar 2023).
Signed a 2021 'fetal heartbeat' abortion ban and a 2022 Texas-style six-week ban enforced by private lawsuits (Mar 2022).
Signed HB 93, Idaho's first private school choice tax credit program, capped at $50 million (Feb 2025).
Signed HB 345 keeping voter-approved expansion but adding work requirements, cost-sharing and managed care, saying it respects voters' will (Mar 2025).
Touted significant teacher pay raises and a 70% rise in state school support during his tenure (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Signed over $400 million in tax cuts in 2025 (May 2025) and proposed conforming to federal tax cuts for seniors and working families (Jan 2026); broad, not middle-class targeted.
His medical debt relief program has erased over $1 billion in medical debt for 500,000+ Illinoisans, per his campaign (2026); the recorded $4 billion figure is not supported.
Signed the Healthcare Protection Act barring prior authorization for in-patient mental health care (2024); campaign also cites lowering insulin costs (2026).
Said data centers should pay any electricity price increase they cause, not consumers (Feb 2026), and proposed a two-year pause on new data center tax credits (Feb 2026).
FY27 budget BUILD plan proposed $50 million through IHDA for first-time homebuyer down payment assistance (Feb 2026).
Created Illinois's first child tax credit (2024) and later doubled it, worth up to $600 a year per his campaign (2026).
BUILD plan would limit local bans on duplexes through four-flats and ADUs, cut parking mandates and streamline permits (Feb 2026 budget address).
Signed SB 208 guaranteeing workers 40 hours of paid leave for any reason (Mar 2023); a narrower PTO mandate, not a family/medical leave insurance program.
Signed the law raising Illinois's minimum wage to $15 an hour by 2025 (Feb 2019); touts it in his 2026 campaign.
Signed the Reproductive Health Act (2019) and further abortion-access expansions, including a Jan 2023 bill and a June 2026 medical-records shield law.
Signed a law banning civil immigration arrests in and near courthouses and requiring hospitals, colleges and day cares to adopt ICE-interaction policies (Dec 2025); no warrant rule.
Campaign credits him with quadrupling Illinois's minimum teacher salary (to $40,000 under a 2019 law) (2026).
Touts expanding preschool and the state's largest early childhood investment; FY27 budget proposed $748 million for the Early Childhood Block Grant (Feb 2026).
Campaign says he lowered child care costs for up to 80% of Illinois families (2026); expanded subsidies, not a universal system.
Championed and gave $56.5M to the 2020 Fair Tax amendment, a graduated income tax with a 7.95% top rate on joint income over $1M; voters rejected it (Nov 2020).
Eliminated the state sales tax on groceries, per his campaign (2026); a consumption-tax cut, not an income tax cut.
Proposed requiring businesses to show full prices upfront and banning hidden mandatory fees (Feb 2026); a general junk-fee ban, not renter-specific.
Opposes abortion rights and, as a senator, publicly cheered the 2022 Dobbs decision overturning Roe v. Wade (Jun 2022).
Said companies that want big power should pay their own way so household bills don't rise (Jan 2026 State of the State); did not address data center tax breaks.
Backed a bill requiring utilities to deliver affordable energy before raising profits and signed HEA 1002 on electric affordability (Jan-Feb 2026); no fee caps or lobbying limits.
Said he backs Rep. Doug Miller's bill to cut regulatory barriers to homebuilding '100%' (Jan 2026) and signed HEA 1001 on housing (Mar 2026).
Led a property tax cut he says saves taxpayers $1.5 billion over three years (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Backed 2026 legislation to keep Hoosiers out of crushing medical debt and curb aggressive collections (Jan 2026); not debt cancellation.
Pushed to codify Medicaid work requirements and signed SEA 1 on human services/Medicaid (Jan-Mar 2026).
Says starting teacher salaries were raised by $5,000 under his administration (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Announced universal school choice for every Indiana family starting fall 2026 (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Wants to lower child care costs, floating a cost-sharing program with businesses (Jan 2026); signed HEA 1177 on child care assistance (Mar 2026).
Touted a crackdown on waste, fraud and abuse saving $465 million (Jan 2026); no inspector general or audit overhaul named.
Pledges to begin reversing Medicaid privatization by executive order on day one, citing illegal care denials (2026 campaign); higher disability-care pay not verified.
Plan would create a Prescription Drugs Review Board to negotiate lower prices on life-saving drugs, including insulin (2026 campaign).
Data center plan requires them to cover 100% of their costs and infrastructure upgrades and ends their state tax breaks (2026 campaign).
Affordability plan would cap utility service/meter fees, make ratemaking more transparent and require regulator approval of utility profit levels (2026 campaign).
Would tax out-of-state landowners at a higher rate (2026 campaign); related idea, not explicitly tied to funding homeowner property-tax cuts.
Proposes universal all-day pre-K funded by ending voucher payments for wealthier families' private tuition (2026 campaign).
Plans to build 21,000 homes by 2030 by easing duplexes, quadplexes and ADUs and simplifying permitting and inspections (2026 campaign).
Supports raising Iowa's minimum wage to $12 an hour (2026 campaign), short of $15; earlier $15 remark not verified.
Would partner with Undue Medical Debt to wipe out Iowans' medical debt at no taxpayer cost and supports removing medical debt from credit scores (2026 campaign).
Would ban landlords from using AI pricing algorithms to fix and raise rents (2026 campaign).
Would make Iowa's first-time homebuyer down payment assistance interest-free instead of an interest-bearing second mortgage (2026 campaign).
Would end voucher payments for wealthier families and add income limits and annual audits to the ESA program, redirecting money to pre-K (2026 campaign); not full repeal.
Would restore the full powers of the state Auditor to find misspent tax dollars and require annual audits of the voucher program (2026 campaign).
Would ban hedge funds and LLCs from buying large amounts of Iowa land (2026 campaign); aimed at farmland, not single-family homes.
